newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to stop stock short sales by foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to stop stock short sales by foreigners.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand will ask institutions providing custodian services not to transfer unpaid stocks to foreign accounts, assistant central bank governor Siri Ganjarerndee said on Tuesday.
The central bank move could help slow selling of Thai stocks by foreign investors who have resorted to short sales of stocks to raise funds in baht, brokers said.

They said heavy turnover posted by the foreign board of the Thai stock exchange on Friday and Monday were attributed to sharply increased short sales made by foreigners who traded stocks borrowed and transferred through custodians.
Brokers said the foreign short sales helped raise temporary baht funds sought by currency speculators for squaring their baht/dollar positions.
Speculators attacking the baht in mid-May have been hurt by Thailand's measure to block foreign access to baht supply through its two-tier baht exchange rate system.
The two-tier system has helped the baht rally strongly in offshore markets in the past few weeks and hurt those seeking baht by selling dollars.
A senior official of the Securities and Exchange Commission said on Tuesday the central bank would also require foreigners dealing in Thai stocks to settle their transactions in U.S. dollars only.
Brokers said the central bank's action to stop transfers of borrowed and unpaid stocks among foreigners would ease volatility in Thai stocks.
